statements.text: Practised two-word requests and waiting for a turn.

citations.quote: Today Asha and I will work on asking for things with two words and on taking turns.
Let us start with the snack game.

statements.text: Ball rolling game to practise turn taking.

citations.quote: Next is the ball rolling game for turn taking.

statements.text: Made four two-word requests without a prompt in the snack game.

citations.quote: In this game she made four two-word requests without any prompt.

statements.text: Waited for her turn in six of ten rolls (60%).

citations.quote: She waited for her turn in six out of ten rolls today, that is sixty percent.

statements.text: Parent reports she uses more words at home this week but still pulls a hand to ask for water.

citations.quote: At home she is saying more words this week.
At home she still pulls my hand when she wants water.

statements.text: Showed the parent how to pause and model "want water" before giving water.

citations.quote: wait and model the words want water, then give it when she tries.
Okay madam, I will wait and say want water first.

statements.text: Snack game at tea time and five minutes of ball rolling each evening.

citations.quote: play the snack game at tea time and roll a ball with her for five minutes each evening.

statements.text: Add colour words to requests (for example "red ball", "blue cup").

citations.quote: Next week we will add colour words to her requests, like red ball and blue cup.
